description: rational resampler 2/3 on real samples vs rational_resampler_fff

fixed_vs_float.rationale: Taps rounded to Q15 (sum of |tap rounding error| 2.2473564014636674e-4) acting on an input peak of 0.705 FS per component, plus 0.5 LSB of output rounding (Q15) and 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference itself; per component <= 5.711716906702882 Q15 LSB. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Taps rounded to Q15 (sum of |tap rounding error| 2.2473564014636674e-4) acting on an input peak of 0.705 FS per component, plus 1.0 LSB of output rounding (Q15) and 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference itself; per component <= 6.211716906702882 Q15 LSB. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Taps rounded to Q17 (sum of |tap rounding error| 5.9154206835085215e-5) acting on an input peak of 0.705 FS per component, plus 0.5 LSB of output rounding (Q17) and 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference itself; per component <= 1.511547359948311 Q15 LSB. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

float_vs_gnuradio.rationale: f32 rounding in an 33-tap sum: each of the n additions errs by at most 2^-24 of the partial sum (<= peak * sum|taps| = 2.1227343886170353); twice that covers both evaluation orders (GNU Radio uses SIMD kernels): 0.2736 Q15 LSB. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

name: rational_resampler_fff_2_3
reference_shift_note: GNU Radio's first output is the full-rate filter output at position (K-1)*I = 32 (K = taps per branch); ours counts from 0 with :phase = 2, so GNU Radio output m is our output m + 10.
